output.summary: The FY2026 record came from the commodity price rally, not from operations. Revenue rose 46.5% while bushels fell 0.9%. Peers with no new program grew revenue 41%, and Cottonwood Prairie ranks 10th of 23 on net savings growth. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K, while the deferred backlog tripled to $1.26M. Harlan Junction has critical insurer findings, including a disconnected bearing sensor and a near-miss closed without the required investigation. Staff report that nothing changes after near-misses, not fear of reprisal. Drying and grading depend on an undocumented, retiring superintendent with no successor. The expansion proposal rests on FY2026 prices, an unsupported volume assumption, and staffing and maintenance plans marked "to follow". Fix the safety issues, start succession, and rebuild the financial case before voting.
